Riobamba lies in Ecuador's central Andes at the foot of Chimborazo volcano. The city stands 2,750 m above sea level. The valley was inhabited long before the Spanish arrived and formed part of the Inca Empire.

The Spanish settlement was founded here on August 15, 1534. Riobamba became the first Spanish city in what is now Ecuador. Colonial buildings stand alongside newer architecture in today's city center.

One of Riobamba's principal historic landmarks is its cathedral. After the earthquake of 1797, surviving sections were moved and reassembled in the center of the new city. The cathedral stands beside a spacious central square near Pedro Vicente Maldonado Park.

A few blocks to the north is the Monasterio de las Conceptas, a museum of religious art housed in a 17th-century convent. Its collection includes icons and ecclesiastical vestments embroidered with gold and silver.

Around Avenida Daniel León Borja, visitors will find restaurants, cafés, bars, shops, art galleries, and souvenir stores. The old part of the city retains spacious squares, historic buildings, and stone-paved streets.

The Riviera Maya lies on Mexico's Caribbean coast. Beach holidays here combine with visits to Maya heritage sites and natural cenotes. The seashore, tropical vegetation, and limestone pools offer varied experiences within one part of the Yucatán Peninsula.

The region includes Tulum, where ancient buildings stand above the sea. After sightseeing, travelers stay at coastal hotels and spend time by the water. The Riviera Maya makes it possible to follow visits to archaeological sites with several days of relaxation, with natural and cultural attractions close at hand.

### Roatán Island

Roatán lies off the northern coast of Honduras, roughly 60 km from the mainland. With green hills, beautiful sandy beaches, and a distinctive reef system extending from the Belize Barrier Reef, the island measures about 64 km long and 6 km wide.

## Holidays on Roatán Island

### Things to Do on Roatán Island

The island's rich underwater life makes diving, snorkeling, and kayaking memorable experiences. Excursions to the butterfly park, the snake and iguana farm, and Carambola Gardens bring their own discoveries. Oak Ridge is particularly striking: like Venice, this small settlement sits on the water, but here a magnificent mangrove tunnel arches its dense branches over one of the channels.

Rongé Island lies off the western coast of Graham Land and forms the western side of Herrera Channel. Its steep slopes and glaciers are clearly visible from the sea, with dark rocks emerging between snow-covered areas.

The island appears on maps made by the Belgian Antarctic Expedition of the late 19th century. It was named in connection with Madame de Rongé, who supported the expedition. Sailing through this area reveals mountainous islands and the peninsula's glaciated coast.
